newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain says social security gap is no deficit risk.
newsitem.headline: Spain says social security gap is no deficit risk.

text.p: Spain confirmed on Tuesday its Social Security revenues would fall short by 200 billion pesetas but said there was no risk of missing its deficit target in the run-up to entry into a single currency.

The budget shortfall, originally announced in May, was the result of a reduction in short-term funding from the previous Socialist government, a spokesman for the Economy Ministry told Reuters. This reduction was part of an extended 1995 budget when the Socialists' 1996 budget was rejected by parliament.
"The 1995 budget had 445.0 billion pesetas of credit available and the previous government cut that by 275.0 billion," the spokesman said.
But the Employment and Social Security Ministry said despite the shortfall, Spain would reach its 4.4 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) 1996 public deficit target.
Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato also said there was no risk that Spain would miss the deficit target.

"I do not know about the reports (of the overshoot) and I won't say anything about other people's statements but I can assure you that there is no risk of missing the (public) deficit target for this year," Rato said at the Franco-Spanish summit in Marseille.
News reports earlier said Spain was considering another budget adjustment before year-end to cover the shortfall.
